newsitem.title: USA: DCR keeps LILCO debt ratings under review.
newsitem.headline: DCR keeps LILCO debt ratings under review.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Monday it has not changed its debt ratings on Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO) but is continuing to monitor them.
Duff & Phelps currently rates LILCO's general and refunding bonds as Triple-B, its debentures and unsecured/unsupported authority financing notes as Double-B-Plus, and preferred stock as Double-B.

LILCO and Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) reached an agreement in principle which would give Long Island customers rate reductions of nearly 20 percent. Under the agreement, LIPA would get various LILCO assets, and in exchange LIPA would buy LILCO stock for about $2.5 billion in cash.
LILCO's remaining assets would become a subsidiary of a new holding company that is expected to be formed upon the completion of its merger with Brooklyn Union Gas.
"While the agreement in principle is a positive step for LILCO, many factors remain unclear and therefore DCR retains LILCO's ratings on Rating Watch -- Uncertain," Duff & Phelps said in a statement.

Duff & Phelps cited uncertainties such as whether LIPA would repay or assume the general and refunding bonds, the impact on LILCO's remaining unsecured debt, and whether both companies can receive a ruling from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service enabling them to complete the deal.
Duff & Phelps said the future credit quality of LILCO would likely depend on various factors, but it now expects it will more likely to hinge on the sale to LIPA.
